source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History Part III, Ch. 10 (Colonialism and the Countryside).

sections.heading: 1. Studying the Countryside — Official Archives
points: The chapter examines how **British colonial rule transformed the Indian countryside**, using **official records/archives** (surveys, reports).
These records are useful but reflect the **colonial (official) viewpoint** — to be read critically.

sections.heading: 2. The Permanent Settlement (Bengal)
points: The **Permanent Settlement (1793, Lord Cornwallis)** in Bengal fixed the land revenue **permanently** with the **zamindars** (made them proprietors).
Aim: a stable revenue and a loyal class of landlords.
Problems: revenue was fixed **too high**; many zamindars **failed to pay** and lost lands (auctions); the **jotedars (rich peasants)** grew powerful; actual cultivators (raiyats) suffered.
The **'Sun-set Law'** — if revenue was not paid by sunset of the due date, the estate was auctioned.

sections.heading: 3. Other Settlements — Ryotwari and Mahalwari
points: **Ryotwari Settlement (South and West India — Thomas Munro)** — revenue settled directly with individual **cultivators (ryots)**; periodically revised.
**Mahalwari Settlement (North-West/Ganga valley — Holt Mackenzie)** — revenue settled with the **village (mahal)** as a unit, collected via the village headman.
All systems maximised revenue for the British and often burdened peasants.

sections.heading: 4. The Santhals and the Deccan Riots
points: **Paharias and Santhals (Rajmahal hills, Bengal)** — the Santhals were settled to clear forests and farm; oppressed by moneylenders/zamindars → the **Santhal Rebellion (1855–56)** led by **Sidhu and Kanhu**.
**Deccan (Bombay) Riots (1875)** — ryots rose against exploitative **moneylenders (sahukars)** amid falling cotton prices (after the American Civil War boom ended) → the **Deccan Riots Commission**.
These reflect the rural distress caused by colonial revenue and debt.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Permanent Settlement (1793, Cornwallis) = fixed revenue with zamindars (Bengal).
Ryotwari (Munro, south/west) = revenue with cultivators; Mahalwari (Mackenzie, NW) = with the village.
'Sun-set Law' = estate auctioned if revenue unpaid by sunset.
Santhal Rebellion (1855–56) = Sidhu and Kanhu.
Deccan Riots (1875) = ryots vs moneylenders (cotton price crash).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Permanent Settlement (1793) = with zamindars (Cornwallis, Bengal)**.
**Ryotwari = with cultivators (Munro)**; **Mahalwari = with the village (Mackenzie)**.
The **Santhal Rebellion (1855–56)** was led by **Sidhu and Kanhu**.
The **Deccan Riots (1875)** were directed against **moneylenders**.
